query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Read reference documents and a spreadsheet, discover fiscal-period logic from available workspace sources, update spreadsheet formulas, and create a summary worksheet.
query_ground_truth.query: inspect spreadsheet structure and batch get cell values for updating formulas
query_ground_truth.rationale: The agent must inspect the spreadsheet layout and retrieve existing cell values simultaneously to understand where and how to update formulas.

request.query: inspect spreadsheet structure and batch get cell values for updating formulas

results.use_case: inspect spreadsheet structure and batch get cell values for updating formulas
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if the spreadsheet identifier is unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Locate the spreadsheet using GOOGLESHEETS_SEARCH_SPREADSHEETS (capture the spreadsheet identifier).
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Confirm exact tab titles using GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES (use exact titles in A1 ranges; wrap titles with spaces/special characters in single quotes).
[Optional (if read/write bounds are uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Fetch grid metadata using GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO (avoid targeting cells outside current dimensions).
[Required] [Step]: Read one or more bounded rectangles using GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_GET (prefer finite ranges; include headers if aligning columns).
[Required] [Step]: Overwrite one or more ranges using GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_VALUES_BATCH (each A1 target maps to a rectangular 2D matrix; use USER_ENTERED when writing formulas).
[Optional (if adding rows without overwriting)] [Next Step]: Add new rows using GOOGLESHEETS_SPREADSHEETS_VALUES_APPEND (use updatedRange/updatedRows to confirm placement).
[Required] [Next Step]: Verify changes by re-reading updated ranges using GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_GET (keep verification rectangles small).
[Fallback (if batch write returns HTTP 400 for one target)] [Fallback]: Retry only the failing range using GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_UPDATE (re-check tab title quoting, A1 range, and 2D matrix shape).
known_pitfalls: [GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES] Tab titles must match exactly in A1 ranges; missing quotes around space-containing titles can trigger HTTP 400 invalid reference.
[GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_GET] valueRenderOption applies to the entire request; separate calls may be needed for formulas vs displayed values.
[GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_GET] Returned rows may omit trailing blank cells/columns, so arrays can be narrower than the requested rectangle.
[GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_VALUES_BATCH] HTTP 400 occurs when the 2D values dimensions don’t match the target A1 range (width/height mismatch).
[GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_UPDATE] Invalid request data can occur when the 2D values matrix contains nulls; normalize nulls to empty strings (or another JSON-safe primitive).

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Normalize a 2D values matrix by replacing nulls before GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_UPDATE
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
def normalize_2d(values):
    return [[('' if c is None else c) for c in (r or [])] for r in (values or [])]
```

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: Google Sheets is a cloud-based spreadsheet tool enabling real-time collaboration, data analysis, and integration with other Google Workspace apps. STRICT RATE LIMITS apply - max 60 reads/minute and 60 writes/minute. Exceeding this causes errors.
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=googlesheets. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="googlesheets") to create a connection BEFORE executing any googlesheets tools.

GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES.description: Lists all worksheet names from a specified Google Spreadsheet (which must exist), useful for discovering sheets before further operations.

exclude_hidden.description: When True, hidden sheets will be excluded from the results. When False (default), all sheets including hidden ones are returned. Hidden sheets are sheets that have been hidden via the 'Hide sheet' option in Google Sheets UI.

spreadsheet_id.description: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet (alphanumeric string, typically 44 characters). Extract only the ID portion from URLs - do not include leading/trailing slashes, '/edit' suffixes, query parameters, or URL fragments. From 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qpyC0XzvTcKT6EISywY/edit#gid=0', use only '1qpyC0XzvTcKT6EISywY'.

GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_GET.description: Retrieves data from specified cell ranges in a Google Spreadsheet.

ranges.description: A list of cell ranges in A1 notation from which to retrieve data. If this list is omitted, empty, or contains only empty strings, all data from the first sheet of the spreadsheet will be fetched. Empty strings in the list are automatically filtered out. Supported formats: (1) Bare sheet name like 'Sheet1' to get all data from that sheet, (2) Sheet with range like 'Sheet1!A1:B2', (3) Just cell reference like 'A1:B2' (uses first sheet). For sheet names with spaces or special characters, enclose in single quotes (e.g., "'My Sheet'" or "'My Sheet'!A1:B2"). IMPORTANT: For large sheets, always use bounded ranges with explicit row limits (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:Z10000' instead of 'Sheet1!A:Z'). Unbounded column ranges like 'A:Z' on sheets with >10,000 rows may cause timeouts or errors. If you need all data from a large sheet, fetch in chunks of 10,000 rows at a time.

majorDimension.description: The major dimension for organizing data in results.

spreadsheet_id.description: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet from which data will be retrieved. This is the ID found in the spreadsheet URL after /d/. You can provide either the spreadsheet ID directly or a full Google Sheets URL (the ID will be extracted automatically).

valueRenderOption.description: How values should be rendered in the output. FORMATTED_VALUE: Values are calculated and formatted (default). UNFORMATTED_VALUE: Values are calculated but not formatted. FORMULA: Values are not calculated; the formula is returned instead.

dateTimeRenderOption.description: How dates and times should be rendered in the output. SERIAL_NUMBER: Dates are returned as serial numbers (default). FORMATTED_STRING: Dates returned as formatted strings.

empty_strings_filtered.description: Indicates whether empty strings were filtered from the response.

GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_VALUES_BATCH.description: Tool to set values in one or more ranges of a spreadsheet. Use when you need to update multiple ranges in a single operation for better performance.

range.description: The A1 notation of the range to update (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:B2', 'Sheet1!C:C', or 'A1:D5'). The range must specify which cells to update.

values.description: The data to write. This is an array of arrays, the outer array representing all the data and each inner array representing a major dimension. Each item in the inner array corresponds with one cell. Supports string, number, boolean, and null values.

majorDimension.description: The major dimension of the values. ROWS (default) means each inner array is a row of values. COLUMNS means each inner array is a column of values.

items.description: Data within a range of the spreadsheet.

data.description: The new values to apply to the spreadsheet. Each ValueRange specifies a range and the values to write to that range. Multiple ranges can be updated in a single request.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet to update. This ID can be found in the URL of the spreadsheet (e.g., https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{spreadsheet_id}/edit). Must be a valid Google Sheets spreadsheet ID.

valueInputOption.description: How the input data should be interpreted. RAW: Values are stored exactly as entered, without parsing. USER_ENTERED: Values are parsed as if typed by a user (numbers stay numbers, strings prefixed with '=' become formulas, etc.). INPUT_VALUE_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED: Default input value option is not specified.

includeValuesInResponse.description: Determines if the update response should include the values of the cells that were updated. By default, responses do not include the updated values.

responseValueRenderOption.description: Determines how values in the response should be rendered. Only used if includeValuesInResponse is true. FORMATTED_VALUE (default): Values are formatted as displayed in the UI. UNFORMATTED_VALUE: Values are unformatted. FORMULA: Formulas are not evaluated.

responseDateTimeRenderOption.description: Determines how dates, times, and durations in the response should be rendered. Only used if includeValuesInResponse is true. SERIAL_NUMBER (default): Dates are returned as numbers. FORMATTED_STRING: Dates are returned as formatted strings.

GOOGLESHEETS_SEARCH_SPREADSHEETS.description: Search for Google Spreadsheets using various filters including name, content, date ranges, and more.

query.description: Search query to filter spreadsheets. Behavior depends on the 'search_type' parameter. For advanced searches, use Google Drive query syntax with fields like 'name contains', 'fullText contains', or boolean filters like 'sharedWithMe = true'. DO NOT use spreadsheet IDs as search terms. Leave empty to get all spreadsheets.

order_by.description: Sort order (comma-separated list for multi-field sorting). Valid fields: createdTime, folder, modifiedByMeTime, modifiedTime, name, name_natural, quotaBytesUsed, recency, sharedWithMeTime, starred, viewedByMeTime. Append ' desc' for descending order (default is ascending). Examples: 'modifiedTime desc', 'folder,name', 'starred,modifiedTime desc'.

page_token.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results. Use the 'next_page_token' value from a previous response to get subsequent pages. Leave empty to get the first page.

max_results.description: Maximum number of spreadsheets to return (1-1000). Defaults to 10.

search_type.description: How to search: 'name' searches filenames only (prefix matching from the START of filenames), 'content' uses fullText search which searches file content, name, description, and metadata (Google Drive API limitation: cannot search content exclusively without also matching filenames), 'both' explicitly searches both name OR content with an OR condition. Note: 'name' search only matches from the START of filenames (e.g., 'Budget' finds 'Budget 2024' but NOT 'Q1 Budget').

starred_only.description: Whether to return only starred spreadsheets. Defaults to False.

created_after.description: Return spreadsheets created after this date. Use RFC 3339 format like '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

modified_after.description: Return spreadsheets modified after this date. Use RFC 3339 format like '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

shared_with_me.description: Whether to return only spreadsheets shared with the current user. Defaults to False.

include_trashed.description: Whether to include spreadsheets in trash. Defaults to False.

include_shared_drives.description: Whether to include spreadsheets from shared drives you have access to. Defaults to True.
